title: Check trail tires before riding
summary: Inspect tread and casing, confirm pressure is within the actual tire/rim system limits, and verify both wheels rotate and seat normally.

steps.title: Inspect tread and casing
steps.instruction: Rotate each wheel and look for cuts, embedded objects, exposed casing, sidewall damage, unusual bulges or severely worn tread.
steps.why: Damage that is easy to see at rest can become a sudden failure once the tire is loaded on trail.
steps.warning: Do not ride a tire with structural casing damage, exposed cords or an unexplained bulge.
steps.check: No obvious unsafe tread or casing damage is visible.

steps.title: Measure pressure rather than guessing
steps.instruction: Measure both tires with a gauge. Compare the readings with the safe limits and setup guidance for the actual tire, rim and bicycle, then adjust as needed for the rider and conditions.
steps.why: A repeatable pressure baseline is more useful than squeezing the tire by hand or copying a universal number.
steps.warning: Respect the lowest applicable pressure/maximum-pressure constraints across the tire, rim and wheel system.
steps.check: Both pressures are measured, recorded if useful, and within the actual system’s safe limits.

steps.title: Check tire seating and rim condition
steps.instruction: Look around the circumference for uneven bead seating, rim damage or signs that the tire is not seated consistently.
steps.why: The tire and rim work as one pressure-containing wheel system.
steps.warning: If a bead is visibly unseated or the rim is damaged, do not simply add pressure and ride.
steps.check: Tire seating appears uniform and no obvious rim damage is visible.

steps.title: Spin both wheels and recheck
steps.instruction: Spin each wheel and watch the tire and rim for obvious wobble, rubbing or unusual movement. Finish with a controlled low-speed check before normal riding.
steps.why: Rotation can reveal problems that are less obvious during a static inspection.
steps.warning: If a wheel, tire or brake behaves abnormally, stop and identify the cause before trail riding.
steps.check: Both wheels rotate normally and the bicycle passes a controlled low-speed check.
